label: Demo page, three elements
note: Choose Multivariate with one row per combination, and untick the conversions column as a factor. The ROI-led headline beats the original by about 0.46 points, and the other elements do not matter.

label: Booking value with mixed formats
note: Values like "$1,234.50", "412,35" and refunds in brackets, with blanks for non-bookers. Read blank as zero and the decimal comma as a decimal; the true difference per visitor is tiny (about +1%) and not significant.

label: A/A test checked every day
note: Both groups are the same, yet checking daily can show a false win. Decide the test length before you start.

label: Day 14 snapshot
note: Type the two rows into the summary table. It looks like a win with p near 0.03, but it is noise from stopping early.

label: Day 21 final result
note: The same test at the planned end. The difference is gone (p near 0.35), which is the honest answer.

label: Tiny sample, 2 versus 9 events
note: 60 visitors per group. A standard test calls it significant, but an exact test gives p of about 0.053, so nine events against two is not enough to act on.

label: Eight variants, one looks best
note: The best variant is up 14% but adjusted for eight comparisons it is not significant. A correct tool says no clear winner.

label: Headline and image crossover
note: Some pairings win and others lose by about 40%, which cancels out on average. Look at the interaction, not just the overall verdict; conversions column is "signups".

label: 90/10 holdout
note: Enter 90,10 as the planned split. With the split declared, the result is clean and not significant; leave it empty and you get a false warning.
